a66a24a77a280f94: MANCHESTER: Manchester City will attempt to keep their perfect Premier League start rolling at home to Ipswich Town on Saturday, with uncertainty over their punishment for financial rule breaches continuing to hang over the leaders.
Enzo Maresca's City have won their opening six league games and sit three points clear of Arsenal, making a fine start on the pitch while their future off it remains unresolved.
An independent commission found City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League. City have denied wrongdoing and lodged an appeal.
The extraordinary backdrop has done little to derail City's domestic campaign. They underlined their strength with a 3-0 victory at 10-man Liverpool last Sunday.
The did lose 4-2 at home to holders Paris St Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday but return to the Etihad Stadium to face an Ipswich side sitting 10th on nine points.

Former Manchester United defender Gary Neville said the uncertainty over City's eventual punishment had created wider frustration around the league, with the club continuing to win while the significance of those victories, with potential sanctions still to come, remained unclear.

"This is not good for the Premier League, this is really bad for the Premier League — it's going to continue for a few months," Neville said on Sky Sports. "Up and down the country, (there's) a lot of annoyance that they see this team win football matches; it's just not going to be enjoyed."
For champions Arsenal, who demolished Lille 3-0 in the Champions League on Tuesday, there is little room to surrender points if they are to keep pace in the title race.
The London side sit second on 15 points and visit Nottingham Forest on Sunday knowing any slip could allow City to open a significant early gap. Forest are 15th with five points.
SPECTACULAR LIVERPOOL VICTORY
Liverpool will arrive at Brentford on Saturday with a different kind of momentum after a spectacular 6-3 Champions League victory at LASK on Wednesday.
The night in Austria belonged to Bradley Barcola, whose hat-trick represented his first goals for Liverpool after going scoreless in his opening six appearances for the club.

The French forward, whose frustrating start with the Reds had drawn increasing scrutiny, struck twice before halftime and completed his treble after the break as Liverpool made it two wins from two in the Champions League.
It was a badly needed breakthrough for 24-year-old Barcola and a welcome response from Liverpool after their humbling home defeat by City four days earlier.

Liverpool have been far less convincing domestically, however. They are ninth on nine points and face a Brentford side sitting a point above them in fourth, meaning Saturday could provide a sterner examination of whether the Reds' nine-goal European thriller has genuinely shifted their momentum.
Manchester United's problems are more acute as they make the short trip to Elland Road to face Leeds United on Sunday desperate to breathe life into a troubled campaign.
Michael Carrick's side have collected six points from their opening six games and sit 13th, already 12 points behind City after their worst start in 40 years.

United slumped to a 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday and their latest assignment carries an additional edge against old rivals Leeds, who have made the stronger start and sit seventh with nine points.

Three teams are still searching for their first victory, including bottom side Fulham who welcome Hull City on Saturday, Bournemouth who host Sunderland on Sunday and Tottenham Hotspur who are at home to Coventry City on Monday.

With Manchester City trying to shut out the noise around their financial case, Arsenal determined to stay on their heels and Liverpool and United searching for a revival, the weekend should help show how the traditional heavyweights are coping. - Reuters

368f7da364907ea6: SYDNEY: Jack Bostock bagged a hat-trick on debut as Australia edged New Zealand 24-22 to kick off their Rugby League World Cup defence with a thrilling victory on Thursday.
The 12-time champion Kangaroos were strong favourites going into the opening match at a sold-out Sydney Football Stadium but they were put through the ringer and only just hung on.
They crossed twice in the first-half but were always on the back foot and lucky to reach the break at 10-10.
With a man in the sin-bin, Australia conceded an early second-half try and looked beaten before Bostock pounced with four minutes left to keep them on track for a fourth consecutive title.
"It was a hell of a battle out there," said Australia captain Isaah Yeo.
"I thought they had a fair bit of ascent in that first-half. We were putting ourselves under a fair bit of pressure, but just felt like for the most part we were really resilient.
"Obviously scored a couple of intercept tries, which probably helped steer us a little bit. But then thought we were able to sort of grind our way back into it in that second half."
It stretched Australia's record over New Zealand to 19 wins and just two defeats.
"That's Test footy, it was a close game, like the full 80 minutes we were battling," said New Zealand skipper James Fisher-Harris.
"Much respect to Australia. Just a few moments went their way, and we fought to the death, which I'm really proud of."
In a big setback, New Zealand could be without superstar Kalyn Ponga for the rest of the tournament with a possible broken arm.
Sensational try
New Zealand applied the early pressure and opened the scoring in spectacular fashion after four minutes through Casey McLean.
The young centre capitalised on a high kick from Jahrome Hughes to somehow dot down in the corner with his body in the air and outside the field of play.
It was a sensational try and Jamayne Isaako curled over a touchline conversion to put the visitors 6-0 ahead.
But the hosts clung on and against the run of play hit back when Dolphins winger Bostock intercepted a stray Hughes pass and sprinted almost the length of the field to haul them into the contest.
Brisbane Broncos' Reece Walsh missed a difficult conversion and then sent a sloppy line drop-out into touch on the full, handing New Zealand a penalty and Isaako made no mistake.

Despite New Zealand applying all the pressure Australia again stunned them with another intercept try, this time from Tom Trbojevic who like Bostock streaked 90 metres to the line and this time Walsh made no mistake.
With the clock ticking to half-time New Zealand drew level when Isaako nailed a penalty that saw the Kangaroos' Kotoni Staggs sent to the bin for a professional foul.
With Staggs on the sidelines, New Zealand piled on the pressure in the second-half and Ponga dotted down after a line break, his first try for the Kiwis after switching allegiance from Australia.
It fired up the hosts and Bostock claimed his second after plucking the ball out of the air at full stretch and riding a collision with Walsh, converting to level at 16-16.
But Ponga then produced some magic, slicing through the defence with his shorts falling down for a converted try to restore New Zealand's lead with 20 minutes left.
Walsh went one better, collecting a flick pass from Bostock and seeing off four defenders for a stunning try in the corner.
He vomited afterwards and was unable to take the kick, with Latrell Mitchell stepping up and missing to leave New Zealand 22-20 ahead with 10 minutes left.
Australia kept coming and Bostock outjumped Isaako at the death to cross for his third to seal the win. - AFP

125a640a53580ba4: BEIRUT: A Hezbollah MP acknowledged Thursday that a 500kg shipment of explosives seized last week by Lebanese authorities belonged to the group, a rare admission by the Iran-backed militants.
"The vehicle and its cargo belong to the resistance" against Israel, lawmaker Hassan Fadlallah said.
He said Hezbollah also called for the immediate release of those arrested over the seizure.
Fadlallah demanded the return of the shipment, seized on a road linking eastern Lebanon to Beirut, saying it constituted "capabilities" used by Hezbollah against Israel.
Lebanese prime minister Nawaf Salam has said the state will no longer tolerate any possession of "illegal weapons".
A judicial source told AFP the explosives were seized from a vehicle that was carrying 250kg of TNT and 250kg of the explosive C-4.
Salam has said authorities will "identify all individuals involved in this criminal operation and those who ordered it".
He said Lebanese people would be concerned by the seizure, especially since C-4 has previously been used in political assassinations in Lebanon.
At the beginning of this decade Hezbollah was accused of carrying out several political killings.
The group, which once dominated political life in Lebanon, has been weakened by two wars it waged against Israel since 2023.
Since a ceasefire in June, Hezbollah has not claimed any further attacks against Israel.
The Lebanese army has seized two other explosives shipments since the beginning of the month in the east of the country, near the border with Syria.
Since the fall of former Syrian president Bashar al-Assad at the end of 2024, the two countries have been working to eradicate smuggling across their porous border.

a27397d20359cfcd: ZURICH: The Asian Cup scheduled for January in Saudi Arabia could be moved back a year to 2028 "if we need to", the continent's top football official said, following a series of Houthi attacks on the country.
But AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa also said they were in "no hurry" to make a decision over Asia's premier football tournament.
The 2027 Asian Cup is supposed to kick off on January 7 in the Saudi cities of Jeddah, Riyadh and Al Khobar.
The kingdom has in recent days come under sustained attack in a dramatic escalation in the war with the Iran-backed Houthi group.
"We can wait until the end of November," the Asian Football Confederation president told reporters in Zurich on Wednesday about a decision on the fate of the Asian Cup.
"Things can change very quickly for better or worse in the region and it is a question of seeing what happens," he added.
"If we need to make a decision then we will, but we could move back a year to 2028 if we need to.
"But at the moment we are monitoring the situation and everything is on schedule."
Cristiano Ronaldo's Al Nassr saw their Asian Champions League match delayed by an hour on Monday after the Saudi-led military coalition said it had intercepted a missile fired towards Riyadh.
Three matches in Saudi domestic football, including one involving Al Nassr, were this week postponed.
The exhibition Six Kings Slam tennis tournament, due to include Novak Djokovic, Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev, was pushed back to the end of December.
Australia, one of the 24 teams set to play at the Asian Cup, said this week it was "closely monitoring" the situation in Saudi Arabia.
The organisation representing South Korean players on Thursday said there was "serious concern regarding the safety of all players participating in the Asian Cup."

"The ongoing military tensions and security instability in the Middle East are issues that cannot be taken lightly," said Lee Keun-ho, president of the Korea Professional Footballers Association (KPFA), according to Yonhap News Agency.
Lee added that "no tournament's value can take precedence over the lives and safety of players and football fans." - AFP
4a6f37fff0fd2d77: HONG KONG: Veteran singer-actor Alex Fong Lik Sun has opened up about the financial struggles he faced during the pandemic.
In a recent web show interview, the 46-year-old revealed that he suffered massive financial losses after investing in non-fungible tokens (NFTs) several years ago.

"The amount was so substantial that I did not dare tell my family. My wife would ask me every day how much I lost and how many digits the amount is. I lost even more money than I did when I invested in stocks previously," he said.
Fong explained that these financial difficulties hit right after he bought a property just before the Covid-19 pandemic.
"I looked at the money left in my bank account and felt frightened. Now, I have managed to recover a little," he said.
Interestingly, Fong admitted that he spent the most money on luxury watches when work was scarce, splashing out HK$100,000 (about RM52,010) to HK$200,000 (around RM104,020) on individual timepieces.
But the star stopped doing so after reading an online article about how people buy expensive items to project success and mask their insecurities.
"I was afraid people would realise that my career wasn't going well, so I spent the most money when I was at my lowest point. Once things started getting better, I had less desire to spend," he said.
Fong now prioritises saving money and building a more stable financial foundation.
"With a wife and a daughter to support, I have to be more cautious.
"If you ask me now, even if I have HK$10, I would only spend HK$6 (about RM3.12) and put the rest elsewhere, without touching the money meant for my family," he said.
Fong also cautioned others against repeating his past investment mistakes.
"I used to want to get rich with one big win, and that was exactly why I lost money," he said.
9889d375a4853d7f: PETALING JAYA: The Court of Appeal today upheld the dismissal of a suit by 21 contractors against the attorney-general, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner and three others over alleged wrongful detention and malicious prosecution.
Bernama reported that a three-member bench comprising Justices Choo Kah Sing, Evrol Mariette Peters and Nadzarin Wok Nordin dismissed the appeal as lacking merit.

Delivering the court’s decision, Choo said the appellants’ complaint – that they had been forcibly detained from Nov 16 to 17, 2014, and held at a place not gazetted for detention under the law – was misplaced.

“With regard to the complaint of malicious prosecution, this court finds that the mere fact that the appellants were found not liable at the close of the prosecution’s case in the sessions court does not equate to malicious prosecution.
“Weak evidence and poor prosecution are not malicious prosecution,” he said.

Choo also said the appellants were charged based on an independent report by the public works department, adding that while the prosecution could have misapprehended the facts or misjudged the strength of the evidence, it could not be concluded that there was no probable or reasonable cause to prosecute the appellants.
He also said the High Court was correct to find the appellants’ claim for false imprisonment was time-barred.
The appellants were arrested by MACC over investigations relating to the alleged misappropriation of funds for a project to repair fishermen housing in 2014.
They were subsequently charged in the Kuala Terengganu sessions court and released on bail on Nov 17, 2014.
On July 31, 2017, the sessions court discharged and acquitted them at the end of the prosecution’s case. The prosecution filed an appeal but subsequently withdrew it on Feb 22, 2019.
Nearly seven years after their arrest, the appellants filed a civil suit against five defendants, including the attorney-general, the MACC chief commissioner, a MACC officer, MACC and the government.
They sought, among others, general damages and aggravated damages of RM1 million each and RM10 million in exemplary damages for all the appellants.
On May 8 this year, the Kuala Terengganu High Court dismissed the appellants’ suit.

Rafaei Adnan and Alif Danial Ahmad Shahrulnizam represented the appellants in the Court of Appeal today, while senior federal counsel Liew Horng Bin and federal counsel Ahmad Faiz Abd Raoff represented the MACC and the government.
effaebc5e166d3b9: TSMC is dispatching personnel to check out US datacenter construction and power availability as it plans billions of dollars in additional chipmaking capacity. The Taiwanese chipmaking giant warned of pressure on consumer markets during its third-quarter earnings call, while maintaining that AI demand - at least for now - continues to outstrip supply. "Looking ahead, we continue to observe consumer and price-sensitive end market segments are being challenged due to the impact of rising component prices and macroeconomic uncertainties. As such, we are being prudent in our business planning going into 2027," said chairman and CEO C.C. Wei. Wei said AI demand remained strong, with CPUs for agentic workloads and networking chips adding to the need for silicon. "Therefore, semiconductors will remain essential in the AI mega trend. The value of semiconductors in the global supply chain is set to continue to increase in our view," he stated. TSMC expects capital expenditure of $60 billion to $64 billion this year. Spending across 2026-2028 is expected to exceed the total for 2023-2025 as it expands capacity for customers. Those plans depend on more than customers ordering chips: the datacenters housing them also need power, networking, memory, and other infrastructure. TSMC is checking how those pieces are coming together before committing to expanding capacity further. TSMC is planning roughly 20 leading-edge manufacturing and advanced-packaging facilities in Taiwan and overseas over the next several years, and Wei said the contract manufacturer is also focusing on capacity optimization across production nodes to generate more wafer output. One analyst on the earnings call asked whether power shortages, datacenter construction delays, advanced-packaging constraints, or limited supplies of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) could hold back projected growth. Wei said TSMC factors these constraints into its capacity planning. "We put every possibility we can, talking about the cloud service providers, capex, datacenter build-out, financial, power supply, and also other component supply, all into our consideration. "We make our own judgment, and then based on our assessment of the demand, we still think the demand is higher than the supply, and we are working very hard to narrow the gap." However, he declined to directly answer a question about whether he expected tightness in the wafer supply to be greater next year than this year, saying "the demand is extremely robust and getting higher and higher." Wei said preparations for A14, TSMC's next-generation process marketed as 1.4 nm, were underway. He expects it to become a bigger business than the current 2 nm generation. Risk production – an initial manufacturing phase ahead of commercial ramp-up – is scheduled for 2027, followed by volume production in 2028. For the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, TSMC reported revenue of $46.72 billion, an increase of 41.2 percent on the same period a year ago. Looking to the fourth quarter, the company expects another jump in revenue, to between $52.3 billion and $54.3 billion. At the midpoint, that would represent roughly 58 percent year-on-year growth. ®

3453ae93e562161b: KUALA LUMPUR: No Malaysians are affected by floods in Istanbul, Turkiye, following unusually heavy rain and strong winds since late Tuesday night.
Malaysian Consul in Istanbul Mardhiah Sabri said the consulate was closely monitoring the situation to ensure Malaysians' safety in the city.

"As of noon local time, no Malaysians have been reported seriously affected. The consulate is also keeping close contact with Malaysian community representatives and student associations to ensure prompt consular assistance if needed.
"Safety advisories have also been issued through the consulate's official channels," she told Buletin TV3.
She said heavy rain since Oct 13 had flooded several parts of Istanbul, affecting roads and residential areas.
Among the worst-hit areas were Beykoz, Sarıyer and Eyüpsultan, which recorded the highest rainfall, as well as Esenyurt and Kağıthane.

"According to the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality's Disaster Coordination Centre (AKOM), rainfall in several districts exceeded 240mm, while wind speeds were forecast to reach between 50 and 80 kilometres per hour.
"However, public transport services have shown signs of recovery, with most closed roads reopened and affected metro and tram services returning to normal.
"Nevertheless, several ferry routes remain cancelled or have been diverted, while a temporary ban has been imposed on motorcycles on city roads," she said.

Mardhiah advised Malaysians in Istanbul, as well as those planning to travel to the city, to follow local authorities' instructions on safety advisories issued through the consulate's official channels.
They were also told to stay away from flooded areas, underpasses and basements, and not to attempt to cross flooded roads.
"Malaysians scheduled to depart for Istanbul are advised to check their flight status with their respective airlines before heading to the airport.
"The Consulate General of Malaysia in Istanbul will continue to monitor developments in coordination with the Turkish authorities and provide Malaysians with the latest updates," she said.

e0b90a443edb35b9: SHANGHAI: Top seed Alexander Zverev took "a huge step up" to dismantle Alex de Minaur 6-4, 6-4 on Thursday and roll into the Shanghai Masters semi-finals.
He will play Alejandro Davidovich Fokina, who advanced when France's Arthur Gea retired injured from their quarter-final after 22 minutes.
Zverev, who will end the year at world number one, was tested by the Australian's speed in the first set but sent down a string of dazzling forehands to convert a break point in the fifth game.
Despite a double-fault the German saved three break points in a row to hold serve and was rewarded in the 10th game, taking the first set with a buttery backhand at the net.
Zverev refused to relent in the second set, setting up another break point in the seventh game to go up 4-3 when De Minaur served into the net.
The 27-year-old Australian clung on for a bit longer but Zverev wasn't sticking around, clinching victory on the first match point.
"Very satisfied with my level... it was a huge step up from the last couple matches."
Zverev needed three sets to win his two previous matches.
France's Gea was in the biggest match of his career when he quit his quarter-final with muscle issues.
The 21-year-old took a medical timeout for work on his lower right side when he was down 1-4 in the first set.
He returned to play but ended the match minutes later.
"I felt this morning, during a warm-up, pain in the psoas," he said, referring to a muscle in the lower back.
He said he received "treatments" and decided to step on court despite being unsure about his fitness.
"I tried from the beginning, but it was not enough to play full and too dangerous for the end of the season.
"I'm really sad, but it's the best choice I could do," said 56th-ranked Gea, who was playing in his first tournament at the prestigious ATP 1000 level. - AFP
73eb85ab5e34b46c: PUTRAJAYA: Mahkamah Rayuan hari ini mengekalkan keputusan Mahkamah Tinggi menolak saman 21 kontraktor terhadap peguam negara, ketua pesuruhjaya Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) dan tiga lagi berhubung dakwaan penahanan salah serta pendakwaan berniat jahat.
Panel tiga hakim terdiri daripada Choo Kah Sing, Evrol Mariette Peters dan Nadzarin Wok Nordin membuat keputusan itu selepas menolak rayuan tersebut atas alasan ia tidak mempunyai merit.

Semasa menyampaikan keputusan mahkamah, Choo berkata, aduan perayu bahawa mereka telah dipenjarakan secara paksa dari 16 Nov hingga 17 Nov 2014 dan tidak ditahan di tempat yang diwartakan bagi tujuan penahanan mengikut lunas undang-undang adalah tidak berasas.

“Berhubung isu pendakwaan berniat jahat, mahkamah ini mendapati hakikat bahawa perayu didapati tidak dipertanggungjawabkan pada akhir kes pendakwaan di Mahkamah Sesyen tidak boleh disamakan dengan pendakwaan berniat jahat.
“Bukti lemah dalam pendakwaan yang tidak berkualiti bukanlah pendakwaan berniat jahat,” katanya.
Hakim itu juga berkata, para perayu telah didakwa berdasarkan laporan bebas yang disediakan oleh Jabatan Kerja Raya (JKR).
Tambahnya, walaupun pihak pendakwaan mungkin tersalah memahami fakta atau tersilap menilai kekuatan bukti, perkara itu tidak bermakna tiada sebab yang munasabah untuk mendakwa kesemua perayu.

Choo juga berkata, Mahkamah Tinggi membuat keputusan yang tepat dengan memutuskan bahawa tindakan undang-undang yang difailkan oleh para perayu berhubung dakwaan pemenjaraan salah telah luput tempoh masa.

Para perayu, terdiri daripada Razali Dollah; Zakaria Jusoh; Rahim Mohamad; Shariman Azam Shafie; Zamri Abdul Mana; Che Forzi Che Abd Aziz; Abdul Rahim Awang; Mohamad Nizam Wahit; Enche Baharuddin Enche Endut; Salim Berahim; Ahmad Atma Ali@Yusof; Abdullah Embong; Othman Omar; Mohd Ramadhan Baharudin; Mohd Amir Ismadi Md Ghani; Mohd Zaid Ahmad@Mat; Mohamad Sari Ngah; Abdul Rashid Muda; Yusof Omar; Fakru Prazi Nordin; dan Shahairi Abd Wahab, telah ditahan oleh SPRM bagi membantu siasatan kes penyelewengan projek membaik pulih rumah nelayan pada 2014.
Mereka kemudian didakwa di Mahkamah Sesyen Kuala Terengganu sebelum dibebaskan dengan jaminan pada 17 Nov 2014.
Perbicaraan kes itu diteruskan dan pada 31 Julai 2017, Mahkamah Sesyen telah membebaskan mereka di akhir kes pendakwaan.
Pihak pendakwaan kemudian memfailkan rayuan sebelum menggugurkannya pada 22 Feb 2019.
Hampir tujuh tahun selepas ditahan, para perayu memfailkan saman dan menamakan peguam negara, ketua pesuruhjaya SPRM, SPRM, kerajaan Malaysia serta seorang pegawai agensi antirasuah itu.
Antara lain, mereka menuntut ganti rugi am dan ganti rugi teruk berjumlah RM1 juta bagi setiap orang serta ganti rugi teladan berjumlah RM10 juta bagi kesemua perayu.
Pada 8 Mei lepas, Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Terengganu menolak saman kesemua perayu.

Pada prosiding hari ini, Mohammad Rafaei Adnan dan Alif Danial Ahmad Shahrulnizam mewakili kesemua perayu manakala Peguam Kanan Persekutuan Liew Horng Bin serta Peguam Persekutuan Ahmad Faiz Abd Raoff hadir bagi pihak SPRM dan kerajaan.

80c01b0aa70e1a76: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia’s gross domestic product (GDP) is expected to grow by 5.2% in 2026 and 4.7% in 2027, amid regional economic uncertainty, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

In its October 2026 Regional Economic Outlook for Asia and the Pacific, themed “Resilient Amid Uncertainty: Can It Be Sustained?”, the IMF highlighted technology-related exports and strong investment in data centres as key contributors to growth across the region.

“Malaysia and Singapore have increased exports as assemblers and packagers of technology products, while strong investment in data centres in China, India, Japan, Indonesia and Malaysia has also contributed to growth,” it said in its report today.
The investment in data centres has generated broader demand for intermediate goods from regional suppliers, including Thailand and Vietnam.
In Malaysia, operational data centre capacity stood at more than 1,000 megawatts (MW), with a further 1,500MW under construction, according to the report.
“As for the composition of services exports, modern services in Malaysia accounted for about 30% of total services exports in 2023, while traditional services made up the remainder.
“Across Asean, services exports embodied in goods exports accounted for 17%, while services exports delivered through a commercial presence accounted for 30%,” the report said.

However, the IMF noted that many services exports in the region remain oriented towards global markets rather than regional markets, particularly modern services, of which only 14%, on average, are exported to countries within the Asia-Pacific region.
On inflation, the report said the pass-through of higher energy prices to both headline and core inflation had remained relatively contained in most advanced and emerging market economies.
“This was partly due to reliance on inventories and the widespread use of price-smoothing measures, including in Malaysia, Korea and Thailand,” it added.

Containing the pass-through of higher energy prices has been the main policy objective, with more than 80% of economies adopting measures to limit the impact on domestic prices, using an average of two to four instruments.
These measures included fuel or utility price freezes and subsidies in Malaysia, alongside fuel tax and duty reductions in Cambodia and Laos, and subsidy-backed fuel price caps in Japan and Thailand.
Targeted support has also complemented broader measures to channel relief to exposed sectors and households. These included credit guarantees or liquidity facilities in Malaysia, India and Singapore.
Demand-side measures, such as work-from-home arrangements, shorter public sector hours and travel restrictions, have also been implemented in Malaysia and several other economies in the region.

On domestic demand, the IMF pointed out that Malaysia's per capita consumption had grown faster than income, with a higher differential than the average among emerging market and developing economies, aided by a notable increase in household borrowing from banks.

For economies where consumption growth was relatively robust, including Malaysia and Thailand, the IMF said policies should focus on strengthening the resilience of consumption, particularly among vulnerable and highly indebted households.

d9be23f4c8dc3b47: WASHINGTON, Oct 15 — One message told him to “go to hell.” Others said he deserved to be imprisoned. Death threats poured in.
Asians who share a name with one of the men accused of raping a US university student have faced a torrent of online abuse.

The alleged 2024 gang rape of a Cornell University student, detailed in a recent lawsuit, has sparked an outpouring of outrage against the seven accused perpetrators. The case has sent internet sleuths scouring digital footprints for clues to track them down.
One of the accused is a Korean man identified by US media as Winston Lee.
The problem is that the world is full of people named Winston Lee.

The rage misdirected at people who share that name, some of whom live outside the US and look nothing like the accused, lays bare the perils of a chaotic internet, where people distrustful of public institutions become digital detectives.

One of those wrongly identified was a Chinese American whose LinkedIn profile identifies him as a New York-based finance professional who graduated from Cornell University in 2020 — four years before the alleged rape.
“You can’t hide. Your future is over,” said one message he received via LinkedIn.
“You’ll get exactly what you deserve...which is prison!! You’ll be gang raped there.”
Another said that a “black magic” spell had been cast upon him.
In a video on TikTok — where his bio reads “Not part of Cornell7” — he said he had hired a lawyer to press charges against a woman who posted his phone number and his parents’ address online.
‘Mob’
After a deluge of hateful messages, another man misidentified as Winston Lee posted a personal appeal to TikTok detectives.
“I am Indonesian and not the Winston Lee named in the recent Cornell University case,” he said.
“Please verify the identity of the person you are looking for before contacting, tagging, or making accusations against someone.”
After a similar flood of messages, a Chinese-American student named Winston Lee at the University of Pennsylvania added a disclaimer to his LinkedIn profile: “I do not go to Cornell.”
Those appeals did not appear to slow what Reddit discussion boards described as an “online hunt” for the seven accused, drawing many users down internet rabbit holes.
With few verified details about the man actually accused, internet users continued searching aggressively for his whereabouts.
One Reddit post claimed Winston Lee was now serving in the South Korean army. Another user on X said she had received tips suggesting Lee had been spotted on Cornell University’s campus.
People with names like the other six accused also complained about rage spamming and threats.
“These social justice warriors are literally messaging and harassing the wrong” people, said podcast host Brad Polumbo.
“These things should be litigated through the criminal process or through some sort of fair process, not through a social media mob or witch hunt.”
‘Hounded’
A group of former Cornell students, who belonged to the same Chi Phi fraternity as the seven accused but graduated before the alleged incident, also complained of online smear campaigns.

“They are being wrongfully accused on social media of having involvement, are consequently receiving death threats and related hate mail,” their attorney Adam Ford wrote in a letter to the university that was obtained by AFP.
“Most of them have had their employers and higher education institutions take adverse actions against them, including being placed on leave.”
Digital sleuths have for years misidentified accused perpetrators of high-profile shootings and other crimes, exposing them to abuse.

Such misidentification can further roil an already chaotic information ecosystem and hinder the actual investigation by generating false leads, warned Mike Rothschild, a researcher who studies conspiracy theories.
“The wrongfully accused are often hounded,” Rothschild told AFP.
“They sometimes have to go into hiding, or get death threats, or are even violently attacked themselves. And there is no penalty for being wrong on the part of those accusing them.” — AFP
5ad004d927d90629: WASHINGTON, Oct 15 — A typhoon in the Philippines and flooding in Brazil. Twice in less than a year, British energy giant Shell has been the target of a new type of lawsuit seeking to make polluters pay part of the cost of specific extreme weather events.
“We chose Shell because it’s an emblematic company. It meets all the criteria,” Thales Miola, a lawyer for the Brazilian NGO Instituto Preservar, told AFP.
On tomorrow, the organisation and federal prosecutors jointly filed a lawsuit against Shell’s subsidiary in South America’s largest country.

They are seeking the equivalent of US$108 million (RM441 million) in compensation for catastrophic flooding in southern Brazil in 2024. The disaster killed nearly 200 people, displaced half a million and caused widespread destruction.
Until now, the only lawsuits filed over the disaster had targeted public authorities.

Shell is not Brazil’s biggest oil company — that distinction belongs to state-owned Petrobras — but it has operated there for decades, and its contribution to global warming is well-documented and “a huge amount for a single company,” Miola said.
According to estimates by the think tank Carbon Majors cited in the lawsuit, Shell holds responsibility for 2.02 per cent of global carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuel and cement-making.
Much of those emissions come from burning the hydrocarbons the company produces and sells. Shell’s share is more than three times that of Petrobras.

At the heart of the legal argument is an attribution study published in a journal belonging to the Nature group, which estimates that climate change intensified the extreme rainfall in 2024 by 12 per cent.
The plaintiffs want Shell to pay for that additional intensity in proportion to its contribution to global emissions: two per cent of the 12 per cent increase.

“In Brazil, it is the first time that we use attribution science against a carbon major company,” Miola said. “Choosing Shell does not exempt the other companies from being prosecuted in the near future.”
Super typhoon
In the Philippines, too, the plaintiffs want Shell to pay for its history and its size.

In December 2021, Typhoon Rai, known locally as Odette, devastated several islands. More than 400 people died and hundreds of thousands lost their homes. It was one of the worst disasters in the country’s history.
Four years later, in 2025, around 100 survivors, supported by NGOs, filed a lawsuit against Shell in the UK, where the company is based.
The lawyers base their case on the company’s “historic carbon emissions” and the link between those emissions and global warming, which climate scientists have shown intensifies cyclones.
Aggravating factor

The plaintiffs cite an additional aggravating factor: Shell’s “history of misinformation regarding the causes and impacts of climate change,” said Greg Lascelles, a lawyer at Hausfeld, the firm handling the lawsuit in London.
“There’s a lot of evidence about Shell knowing as early as in the 1960s” that fossil fuels contributed to global warming, said Madeleine Lynch, a campaigner on the “Odette case.”
The lawsuit argues that this establishes negligence under Philippine law.
The Brazilian lawsuit also cites Shell’s past record, including an internal company report from 1986 that acknowledged fossil fuels’ role in increasing greenhouse gas emissions and global warming.

Shell has not responded to the Brazilian lawsuit. However, in December, following the Philippine lawsuit, the company said “the suggestion that Shell had unique knowledge about climate change is simply not true.”
‘Test cases’
Claims seeking compensation from major companies for specific climate-related damage — sometimes in countries where those companies are not even based — are only just beginning to emerge.
Swiss cement maker Holcim is being sued by residents of an Indonesian island being eroded by rising sea levels. Pakistani farmers are suing two companies in Germany, including a cement manufacturer.

“The cases we’re seeing in the world are test cases, to see whether it is a viable legal strategy,” said Noah Walker-Crawford, a researcher at the Grantham Research Institute on Climate Change and the Environment at the London School of Economics.
“If these cases are successful,” he said, “We could expect to see a lot more of these cases against more companies as well.” — AFP

3cc458205013dac6: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Healthcare Travel Council (MHTC) and Malayan Banking Bhd have entered into a multi-year partnership to improve access to Malaysia’s healthcare services for Maybank customers across Asean.

The collaboration will connect Maybank’s regional customer base with MHTC’s healthcare network, providing information on medical treatment, healthcare facilities, and support services available in Malaysia. The initiative is expected to expand into additional priority markets from 2027.
The partnership builds on MHTC and Maybank’s joint participation at MH WellFest Cambodia 2026 in early October, where Malaysian healthcare workers delivered health talks and personal consultations.
Indonesia, the Philippines, and Singapore have been identified as priority markets for the next phase of the initiative.
MHTC chief executive officer Suriaghandi Suppiah said seeking medical treatment abroad involves more than choosing a hospital.
Patients must also navigate unfamiliar healthcare systems, manage costs, and make arrangements for accompanying family members.
He said that while Malaysia has 91 MHTC-accredited healthcare facilities, ensuring patients can reach and use those services is just as important.
“Quality alone does not bring a patient to our door. Access does,” Suriaghandi said at the signing ceremony at Menara Merdeka Maybank.

“We will build on what we have learned in Cambodia, refine it together, and measure what works. Where the results support it, we will take this approach to other priority markets across Asean from 2027,” he said.
The initial rollout will see Maybank Premier clients in Cambodia access healthcare and wellness information through MHTC’s network.
In Indonesia, customers will have access to healthcare-related privileges and support.
MHTC will also help Malaysian private hospitals reach more international patients through Maybank’s Asean customer base.

Maybank group chief executive officer of community financial services Syed Ahmad Taufik Albar said the collaboration reflects the bank’s efforts to support customers whose needs increasingly extend beyond conventional banking.

“Across Asean, our customers lead increasingly mobile lives, with needs and priorities that extend across markets. With a banking network spanning 10 Asean countries, Maybank is well-positioned to meet these evolving needs in ways that go beyond traditional banking,” he said in a joint statement.
The partnership supports the Malaysia Year of Medical Tourism 2026 initiative and the health ministry’s efforts to strengthen Malaysia’s position as a preferred medical tourism destination.
197cac23ab866ba2: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the Universiti Malaya (UM) Student Residence project to serve as a model for development management that is clean, efficient, and free from leakages or the wastage of public funds.

He said the implementation of this project must draw lessons from the shortcomings of past project management which led to cost overruns, delays, and abandoned construction sites ultimately resulting in losses for the nation.

“How much national funding has been wasted or lost due to poor management? Therefore, vice-chancellor, ensure that UM and this Student Residence project become an example for other agencies to emulate.

“You can do a great job, a clean job, an incorruptible job, and one carried out with full dedication. This is a real challenge for us,” he said during his inaugural address at the launch of the UM Student Residence project here today.

Also present were Minister of Higher Education Datuk Seri Dr. Zambry Abd Kadir and his deputy, Adam Adli Abd Halim; Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar; and UM vice-chancellor Prof Datuk Seri Dr Noor Azuan Abu Osman.

Anwar said the project in question is a major responsibility that must be carried out with full dedication, requiring the commitment of all involved parties to ensure it is completed according to plan.

He noted that the issue of “leakages” (inefficiencies or losses) does not stem from differences in race, region, or social class; rather, it is linked to dishonest conduct that undermines the national interest.

Consequently, the Prime Minister said he would personally oversee the project’s implementation. He also expressed his desire for it to be completed ahead of the original 2030 schedule, aiming to address the issue of student accommodation specifically the rising cost of house rentals in areas surrounding universities.

To ensure the project is expedited, Anwar said he has directed all government machinery including government-linked companies (GLCs) and government-linked investment companies (GLICs) to prioritise this initiative.

“This is a priority project for us that must be completed quickly. When you (Azuan) say it will be ready by 2030, I say no. This is a new, efficient Madani government. We will work to ensure it is accelerated,” he said.

Designed to accommodate 40,000 students, the project will be executed in phases: Phase One will cater to 10,000 students, followed by Phase Two, which will provide additional capacity for another 30,000 students.

The residences will offer four categories of accommodation: ‘Standard’ (five rooms for 10 residents), ‘Standard Premium’ (three rooms for six residents), ‘Apartment’ (two rooms for three residents), and ‘Studio’ (for a single resident). All units are planned to be equipped with air-conditioning.

The project is based on a ‘community living’ concept, integrating residential functions with spaces for social interaction and community activities. This aims to foster an environment that encourages character development, social connections, and a sense of togetherness, thereby enriching the students’ overall experience throughout their studies.

Meanwhile, Deputy Minister of Higher Education Adam Adli Abd Halim, speaking to reporters after the event, expressed hope that this initiative would serve as a long-term, sustainable solution to issues concerning student accommodation.
He said the government is committed to ensuring the project proceeds smoothly through a ‘fast-track’ approach, without compromising on integrity or established management procedures.

“This project begins at UM, Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), and Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin (UniSZA), with a second phase to follow. I believe we can expand this programme to other universities as well,” he said.

Earlier, in his speech, Azuan said the development of the Student Residences (*Residensi Siswa*) reflects the university’s commitment to prioritising student welfare, alongside its efforts to strengthen academic and research excellence.

“We cannot speak of excellence in higher education without addressing the realities of student life. The need for comfortable, safe, and affordable housing must be a core priority in the university’s development agenda.

“Through the Student Residences, UM aims to ensure that campus development is not focused solely on academic infrastructure, but also delivers tangible benefits to the daily lives of its students,” he said. — Bernama

643cefd751f443e5: KUALA LUMPUR: The Housing and Local Government Ministry is studying a proposed option-to-purchase (OTP) mechanism to reduce sick and abandoned housing projects and better protect homebuyers.

Its minister Nga Kor Ming said the mechanism would introduce a more structured process before sale and purchase agreements are signed, allowing developers to gauge genuine demand while safeguarding buyers' interests.
"At present, developers often assess market demand through the collection of booking fees.

"However, this presents several challenges, including difficulties in distinguishing genuine buyers from those who are not serious about purchasing, while homebuyers risk losing their booking fees if they choose not to proceed," he said.
Under the proposed mechanism, developers would be given a specified period to assess buyer interest before deciding whether to proceed.
Buyers could pay up to five per cent of the proposed purchase price and submit their financial information for loan assessments.
If the developer decides not to proceed, buyers would receive a full refund together with accrued interest.
Through the proposed OTP mechanism, developers would be required to honour the indicative price initially offered to buyers, ensuring that the final selling price remains unchanged.
"For developers, this means greater certainty over genuine market demand. For homebuyers, it means greater transparency and price certainty before making a major financial commitment.
"Through this reform, we want to ensure that buyers will never have to pay for houses that they will never get," he said at the 5th Malaysia Developer Awards 2026 on Wednesday.
Meanwhile, Nga said the ministry secured a larger allocation under the 2027 Budget to implement big data analytics to address housing supply-demand mismatches.
This follows an 8.6 per cent increase in completed but unsold residential units in the first half of 2026.
The initiative would also support the government's target of delivering one million affordable homes over the next decade under the National Housing Policy 2026–2035.

4c750a29167cd0ac: PETALING JAYA: The housing and local government ministry is looking into a mechanism to provide greater protection for homebuyers and reduce the risk of sick and abandoned private housing projects.
Minister Nga Kor Ming said the proposed "option to purchase" (OTP) mechanism would establish a more systematic process before the signing of the sale and purchase agreement (SPA).
The OTP mechanism aims to safeguard homebuyers' interests while allowing developers to better assess genuine market demand, he said.
Under the OTP mechanism, developers would be given a specified period to assess buyer interest before deciding whether to proceed.
Buyers, on the other hand, could pay up to 5% of the proposed purchase price and submit their financial information for loan assessments.
Should the developer decide not to proceed, buyers would receive a full refund together with accrued interest.
"At present, developers often assess market demand through the collection of booking fees.

"However, this presents several challenges, including difficulties in distinguishing genuine buyers from those who are not serious about purchasing, while homebuyers risk losing their booking fees if they choose not to proceed," Nga said in a statement.
Nga also said that the mechanism would also provide greater price certainty for homebuyers.
Currently, buyers may pay booking fees based on an indicative price, only to discover that the final selling price has changed when the project is launched, he said.
Nga said through the proposed OTP mechanism, developers would be required to honour the indicative price initially offered to buyers, ensuring that the final selling price remains unchanged.
"For developers, this means greater certainty on genuine market demand.

"For homebuyers, it means greater transparency and price certainty before making a major financial commitment. Through this reform, we want to ensure that buyers will never have to pay for houses that they may never get."

Nga also encouraged established developers to step forward as white knights to revive abandoned projects, noting that the 2027 budget proposed full stamp duty exemptions on qualifying loan agreements and property transfers involving developers coming to the rescue and the original homebuyers.

a1fa1e4475e5ba83: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has reverted to the National Haze Action Plan (PTJK) guidelines, which mandate the immediate closure of schools when the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaches 200, following input from various relevant agencies.
Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said that under the PTJK, all outdoor classroom activities must also be halted when the API exceeds 100.
She added that parents are also permitted not to send their children to school if they are concerned that the haze condition could affect their health, provided they notify the school administration.
“In managing the haze, specific actions must be taken for each API reading level. We cannot assume that all risk levels require the same course of action,” she said in a Facebook post today.

She noted that the decision to return to the PTJK guidelines was made after discussions with related agencies, including taking into account views from the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) that haze management must be guided by the said plan.

Fadhlina stated that the previous decision to take a more cautious approach was made by taking seriously the concerns expressed by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia regarding the haze situation, while prioritising the safety and health of students.

According to her, the MOE also received various feedback from parents, including requests for schools to be closed for a week, concerns about learning gaps, and the difficulty of managing childcare while working.

Therefore, she said the ministry called upon all relevant agencies such as the Ministry of Health, the Department of Environment (DOE), and the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) for discussions, as the issue involves health, air quality, and disaster management that require their expertise.
“I understand that logic. After all, an API reading of 150 is indeed within the unhealthy category. Parents’ concerns at that level are certainly well-founded,” she said.

Fadhlina stated that the flexibility given for students to be absent from school takes into account differing health conditions among students, including those suffering from asthma, respiratory issues, or those more easily affected by the haze.

She said the MOE is also responsible for ensuring that students do not continuously lose learning time, drawing from the experience during the Movement Control Order (MCO) which highlighted the difficulty of recovering missed learning, while emphasising that every concern will continue to be heard and decisions made in consultation with expert authorities. — Bernama

6fbf58318fbffd9d: HONG KONG: Popular comedienne Sandra Ng, best known for starring alongside "King of Comedy" Stephen Chow in numerous hit films and dramas, recently had a big scare involving her blood pressure reading.

Ng, 61, who is usually in good health and monitors her blood pressure daily, saw her readings shoot up to an alarming level while filming the Chinese travel reality show Divas Hit the Road 2026 in Mexico.
According to 8Days, a recent episode saw Ng and her fellow cast members—Ariel Lin, Zhou Dongyu, Yin Tao, Deng Wei, and Wang Xingyue—visiting a historic pyramid.

She went back to the tour bus, took off her heavy outerwear, applied ice packs to cool down, and drank plenty of water, but the persistent headache would not shift.
Medical personnel were called to examine her and recorded her blood pressure at 159/102 mmHg, pointing to severe hypertension.
A healthy reading is typically below 120/80 mmHg, whereas anything from 140/90 mmHg upwards is classed as high.
Ng was stunned and confessed she was frightened by the sudden spike, which was believed to have been brought on by altitude sickness.
When Yin Tao, Lin, and Deng Wei later returned to check on her, Yin Tao helped Ng position her arm properly before checking her blood pressure once more.
This time, the reading was even higher: 174/93 mmHg.
Thinking the monitor might be faulty, Deng Wei, Wang Xingyue, and Yin Tao took turns testing the device on themselves.
Turns out, the machine was working just fine.
Ng later joined the group for a meal, where another check showed her systolic pressure was still at 174 mmHg, though her diastolic pressure had dropped to 67 mmHg.
Taking no chances, the production team sent her straight back to the hotel to rest.
Thankfully, by the next day, Ng's blood pressure had settled back to a healthy 120/76 mmHg, and she was feeling like herself again.

3a9f4367bfa4c83a: Rocket Lab has delayed the maiden launch of its Neutron rocket again, due to carbon composite manufacturing issues. It is more than five years since Rocket Lab said it was developing the launcher, a step up from its workhorse Electron, and capable of sending up to 13,000 kg to Low Earth Orbit. At the time, 2024 was mooted as the first launch date. Then perhaps 2025. Then 2026. And now it is "expected to occur in 2027." It won't be early in 2027 either. During a briefing, boss Peter Beck said he expects to complete testing of the problematic components before the end of Q1 2027, at which point it will set a new launch date. According to Beck, Rocket Lab identified problems with a first-stage tank that failed qualification due to third-party processing. The space biz switched to its own internal processes, and things appeared to be going swimmingly until, Beck said, "we identified an issue with the manufacturing process for the propellant dome." The issue was voids that formed within the carbon composite layers during manufacturing. Beck explained, "They don't necessarily mean that the dome would fail in flight," but they would reduce the margin, so a rethink was required. The good news, according to Beck, is that the problem is solved. The bad news? Dealing with it has delayed things. In August, Rocket Lab said it targeted delivery of Neutron to the launch pad in Q4 2026. Beck now reckons the cryo and hydrostatic test campaigns will not wrap up until Q1 2027. Rocket Lab's shares have taken a battering following the announcement, dropping from about $63 yesterday to near $53 in after-hours trading. When it becomes operational, Neutron will feature an entirely reusable first stage with a "Hungry Hippo" clamshell fairing, opening to deploy a second stage before closing for a return to Earth. The timing of Neutron's availability is of note since it could come as SpaceX reportedly seeks to wind down Falcon 9 in favor of Starship. While Falcon 9 can loft heavier payloads, Neutron's mass capability puts it firmly in the same class. Assuming, of course, it makes it to the launchpad. ®

The results are a big milestone. But the team still needs to establish whether the approach could work for humans.

b442b1e0805f9c1f: GWM Malaysia has added two dealerships in Johor and Selangor as vehicle deliveries rose 33 per cent year-on-year to 5,165 units in the first nine months of 2026.

The 22,006 sq ft facility combines sales, service and spare parts operations, with three service bays and capacity to service about 150 vehicles a month.
It also has five vehicle display spaces, an electric vehicle charging station, diagnostic equipment and a dedicated vehicle delivery bay.
The outlet supports about 40 jobs across sales, technical, service and customer support functions.
Customers can view and test-drive selected models including the Haval H6, Wey G9, Tank 300, Tank 500 and Ora Good Cat.
Auto Elegance managing director Yang Ce said the company saw potential for the brand in Johor and wanted to build long-term relationships with local customers.
"We are proud to expand our partnership with GWM into Johor Bahru," he said, adding that the outlet aimed to provide customers with support from vehicle purchase through ownership.
GWM Equine Park, operated by Golden Admiral Motors Sdn Bhd, was officially opened on Oct 10, although its showroom began operations in April and its service centre opened in August.

The showroom can accommodate at least seven vehicles, while the 3,661 sq ft service centre has four vehicle hoists, wheel-alignment and tyre-balancing equipment, and diagnostic facilities for internal combustion engine, hybrid, plug-in hybrid and electric vehicles.
Golden Admiral Motors managing director Datuk William Chang Yoong Hsi said the company had invested in facilities, equipment and staff to support customers over the longer term.

"Our goal is that every customer should feel welcomed, listened to and properly supported from the first vehicle enquiry and test drive to vehicle delivery, scheduled servicing and long-term ownership," he said.
GWM Malaysia managing director Stan Li Hao said network growth needed to be matched by consistent service standards.
"Our priority is not simply to add more locations, but to make our products and services more accessible while delivering a consistent experience at every customer touchpoint," he said.

Chief operating officer Roslan Abdullah said the company was also strengthening technical training, parts availability and dealer operating standards as its range expands across different powertrain technologies.
"A strong ownership experience depends on what happens after the vehicle leaves the showroom," he said.

a3ad638751a457f8: JOHOR BARU: Behind the car radio, inside door panels and beneath the boot lining, almost every hollow space in a Malaysia-registered car was used to conceal contraband cigarettes bound for Singapore.
The elaborate concealment failed at Woodlands Checkpoint on Oct 5, when Singapore's Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) officers stopped the vehicle for enhanced checks.
They uncovered more than 700 cartons and 2,000 packets of duty-unpaid cigarettes.
The 32-year-old Malaysian driver was arrested, and both him and the seized cigarettes were referred to Singapore Customs.
Despite Singapore's tough stance on contraband, cigarette smuggling attempts persist, driven by the lucrative black market.
The seizure highlights persistent cigarette smuggling attempts despite Singapore's tough stance on contraband, with high tobacco taxes creating a lucrative market for illicit cigarettes.
As a price benchmark, cartons of 10 packets of premium cigarettes in Singapore can retail for S$160 (about RM509).

At that price, 700 cartons and another 2,000 packets would have a hypothetical legal retail value of about S$144,000 (RM458,000). However, the actual value would depend on the brands involved, their purchase costs and the prices charged on the illegal market.

The latest interception follows a similar case in August, when ICA officers at Woodlands Checkpoint found more than 700 cartons and over 100 packets of duty-unpaid cigarettes hidden in modified compartments of another Malaysia-registered car.
The repeated attempts come despite stiff penalties for cigarette smuggling in Singapore.
Under the Customs Act and Goods and Services Tax Act, offenders dealing in duty-unpaid cigarettes can face fines of up to 40 times the duty and GST evaded, imprisonment of up to six years, or both.
Vehicles used in such offences and proceeds from the illegal trade may also be forfeited.
13c6a7d378d127a2: SAN FRANCISCO: Tesla is set to unveil its redesigned Roadster on Thursday, nearly nine years after it first showed a next-generation version of its electric sports car.
Tesla revealed a prototype of the US$200,000 car in 2017 and said deliveries would begin in 2020.
The price has not been updated, but reservations are still US$50,000 each.
Chief Executive Elon Musk has played down the car's importance to Tesla's finances, describing it in 2023 as a "small potato situation" that would not "move the needle in a major way financially".
However, the car still carries symbolic weight.
"Tesla does not currently have a halo car, or high-performance luxury vehicle designed to showcase an automaker's best engineering and technology.
"The Roadster will be Tesla's new halo car," Morningstar analyst Seth Goldstein said in a note last month.
Musk set expectations in 2017, saying a four-seat Roadster would travel 1,000km on a single charge.

In 2024, he posted on X that it had been redesigned. The new Roadster would accelerate from 0 to 100km per hour in less than a second. "And that is the least interesting part," he wrote, adding it was a collaboration between Tesla and SpaceX, the rocket company Musk also leads.
Goldstein expects Tesla to sell around 2,000 Roadsters a year — a fraction of the 1.6 million vehicles Tesla sold last year.
The original Roadster, released in 2008 and on sale until 2012, was Tesla's first-ever EV and used a Lotus Elise chassis.
It helped change the world's view of what an electric vehicle could be. The company has since been known for its Model Y and Model X SUVs and Model S and Model 3 sedans.

The reveal of the second-generation Roadster also comes amid a sharp shift in Tesla's focus to artificial intelligence-led self-driving tech and robotics, away from manufacturing cars for human drivers.

This year, Tesla stopped selling Model S and X vehicles to make space for production of its Optimus humanoid robots. It also launched Cybercab - a two-seater robotaxi that comes without manual controls such as a steering wheel, pedals and mirrors.
The Roadster event is set to start at 8.55pm today at a SpaceX ​test site in McGregor, Texas.

81d2949c150afaeb: REMBAU: Malaysia has no plans to send a diplomatic note or take legal action against Indonesia over the transboundary haze currently affecting the country, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He said such action was unnecessary as it could affect the good relations between the two countries.
"We have not reached that stage (of sending a diplomatic note). It is easy to say so in parliament, but if we were to do that, it would mean we were prepared to sever diplomatic ties.

"We need to safeguard the close relationship between the two countries. So, we are not going as far as sending a diplomatic note or taking legal action," he told reporters at Dewan Orang Ramai Rantau.

He was responding to a call by Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman for the government to take action against Indonesia, including lodging a diplomatic protest over open burning in the country that has contributed to the haze.

Syed Saddiq was reported to have said the government should not rely solely on meetings with Indonesian leaders, but should issue a clear diplomatic note with the support of other affected Asean countries, particularly Singapore.
Mohamad, who is also Rembau MP, said sending a diplomatic note was not the best way forward, as Malaysia had to take its relationship with Indonesia into account.
He said such a move might be a last resort, adding that Malaysia was currently opting for discussions and diplomacy to address the issue.
"A more appropriate approach is through diplomacy, which is the best way forward rather than sending a diplomatic note.
"I have discussed this with my counterpart, while the prime minister and deputy prime minister have also contacted the Indonesian president to discuss the matter," he said.
df24ff35c43b5cb4: KUALA LUMPUR: Genting Plantations Bhd's property arm has partnered with Huawei Technologies (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd to masterplan a 174-hectare smart campus in Johor, marking the Chinese technology group's first international smart campus partnership.

6801b5585a05d9fc: BENGALURU: The ATP outlined plans on Thursday to substantially boost its bonus pool and reshape its rankings and calendar from 2028 under a package projected to lift player compensation to US$350 million while seeking to ease growing concerns over player workload.

The men's and women's tours have faced mounting criticism over their demanding 11-month seasons, while players have pushed for a greater share of revenue and better welfare benefits amid wider concerns about the demands and costs of competing.

Under proposals presented by ATP Chairman Andrea Gaudenzi, the men's tour's bonus pool would rise from US$21.5 million to $50 million, with another US$25 million for year-end top-250 players and US$30 million annually for pensions covering 300 players.
"Tennis is in a strong position today," Gaudenzi wrote in an open letter released on Thursday.
"Our events continue to grow, fans are engaging with the sport in more ways than ever and player earnings have reached record levels. To stay strong, the sport has to keep evolving.
"We have a responsibility to strengthen competition, better align incentives and extend support to more players, helping them to address the costs of competing on the tour."
Clearer structure for tour

Subject to further consultation and approval, the ATP's central player compensation would exceed US$100 million from 2028, with prize money and profit-sharing taking total player compensation to a projected US$350 million before any Grand Slam prize money is taken into account.

The ATP also plans to give results at its biggest events greater rankings weight, reducing the incentive for players to chase points elsewhere after poor performances, while creating dedicated tournament-category weeks for a clearer structure.
The new ATP Masters 1000 tournament in Saudi Arabia will form part of that structure, with the ATP adding that players remained free to compete across the full breadth of the tour.
Players have become increasingly vocal about the physical toll of the season, arguing that the relentless schedule leaves too little time for recovery and increases the risk of fatigue and injury.

The rankings system has also come under scrutiny, with some players arguing that the pursuit of points can encourage them to keep competing even at non-mandatory events, making it harder to carve out meaningful breaks during the season.

The ATP said it would review the long-term structure of its competition formats, including potential changes to its doubles draws, with any prize money reallocated expected to go towards singles qualifying and early-round payouts.

Earlier this year, doubles players reacted angrily to suggestions that the tour planned to reduce the size of draws at tournaments, with the ATP arguing that it was looking at ways to create a more sustainable long-term model for the format.
More coherent to all

Gaudenzi, 53, who in February was re-elected for a third term through 2028, said the ATP's proposals would help players plan their seasons better, reward performances at the biggest events and broaden support.

The Italian added that the ATP would continue developing the proposals with its player and tournament advisory councils and board, aiming to bring a final package forward at its year-end meetings in Turin.
"OneVision has already helped strengthen our tour and the sport of tennis," Gaudenzi said of his organisation's long-term strategic plan.
"The next phase is an opportunity to make the season more coherent for players and fans and to ensure that the growth of the sport creates opportunity across the tour.
"Our immediate focus is the ATP Tour, but the ambition reaches further: ensuring tennis wins the competition for the next generation of fans."
77aa97fae2c6a60f: PETALING JAYA: A 27-year-old swimming coach has been arrested by police, who also seized RM6.8 million worth of drugs, during enforcement action in Melaka and Johor.

Robert said the raid in Johor was conducted around 4.50am today at a residential unit in Crescent Bay Suites, Johor Bahru, where police found various types of drugs and equipment, believed to have been used to pack and store the drugs.
He went on to reveal that the suspect, who tested positive for ketamine, was involved in the collection, packing and handling of the drugs.

cca602259dec04d3: ISTANBUL, Oct 15 — Istanbul was today battling to recover from flooding caused by what officials said was the heaviest rainfall in the city since records began more than 80 years ago, as the downpour continued.

The rain began lashing Turkey’s largest city in earnest yesterday morning and intensified throughout the day, causing chaos and flash flooding, with footage showing cars being dragged away by the fast-flowing waters.
“We are talking here about the highest level of precipitation in Istanbul since records began in 1942,” Istanbul governor Davut Gul said.

Two people died in the floods, one of them a 14-year-old boy who was electrocuted when he stepped into a puddle in the Balat area. He was rushed to hospital but medical personnel were unable to save him, officials said.
Another three people were being treated in hospital, Gul said.

On yesterday evening, the governor said schools would be shut across Istanbul until Monday, urging people to stay home “unless absolutely necessary” and advising those living in basement properties “to spend the night on safer, higher floors”.
He advised residents to stay away from “stream beds, underpasses and other areas at risk of flooding”.
Dramatic footage posted online and collated by DHA news agency showed a line of parked cars in the northern Sariyer district being pushed into the torrent of muddy water, where they were swept away.

Another showed people being hauled from the raging waters to safety through a first-floor window, while elsewhere two people with umbrellas were seen stepping into the shovel of a large mechanical digger, which took them away.

Forty-three flights bound for Istanbul Airport on the Black Sea had to be diverted, as did three flights heading for the city’s Sabiha Gokcen airport on the Asian side, which also temporarily suspended take-offs due to strong winds, the transport ministry said in a statement carried by state news agency Anadolu.

Turkey’s AFAD disaster agency has set up a crisis desk to manage incidents caused by the heavy rainfall, which by nightfall yesterday had risen to 1,277 flooding incidents, 15 landslides, 47 people stranded and two roofs blown off.
The heavy rains are expected to continue over the weekend. — AFP

98ed15fcaf111b1f: Apple's trade secrets spat with OpenAI has taken a new turn, with the ChatGPT maker accusing a former employee of taking more than 100 confidential files about its unreleased hardware back to Cupertino. In a court filing submitted Wednesday, OpenAI claims the unnamed employee, who joined from Apple before returning to the iPhone maker just six months later, transferred sensitive documents to his personal accounts before leaving. The filing alleges the files included detailed images of at least one unreleased OpenAI device, engineering and manufacturing data, supplier information, and project files, along with specifications for cosmetic finishes and reports on coating and sealing hardware components. According to the filing, some were transferred just after midnight in Singapore on June 2, which the filing claims was the employee's final day at OpenAI. But OpenAI claims the information didn't simply disappear into a personal inbox. According to the filing, the former employee also allegedly presented OpenAI's product plans to Apple's senior leadership, including its vice president of operations in Asia. That presentation apparently happened months ago, and OpenAI is now pointing to Apple's latest push into AI-powered hardware, including its newly announced smart home products, as cause for concern. "OpenAI is very concerned that its trade secret and confidential information is now circulating inside Apple, where Apple engineers can shape Apple's upcoming products based on OpenAI's confidential and innovative work," the company told the court. Apple says it hasn't found anything to back up OpenAI's claims and insists it has rules to stop staff from bringing their former employers' secrets into the company. There's a certain irony here, given that Apple was the one accusing OpenAI of stealing its secrets just a few months ago. Back in July, Apple sued OpenAI and former employees Chang Liu and Tang Yew Tan, alleging they took confidential engineering information to help the ChatGPT maker develop its own hardware. Cupertino alleged that the pair took valuable trade secrets concerning its hardware development, including information about unreleased products, to their new employer. OpenAI denied the accusations, saying at the time: "We have no interest in other companies' trade secrets. We remain focused on building innovative technology that empowers people everywhere." Now the ChatGPT maker is claiming confidential hardware information may have traveled in the opposite direction, though it has yet to establish that Apple received or used any of the allegedly taken material. OpenAI has asked the court for time to investigate the matter and potentially bring counterclaims against Apple. No such counterclaims have yet been filed. For all the talk of groundbreaking AI hardware, the biggest competition right now appears to be over who took whose files. ®
