25300692a04a760a: PUTRAJAYA: A book titled Anwar Ibrahim: A Life Recorded (Anwar Ibrahim: Kisah yang Dirakam), chronicling the life, struggles and leadership journey of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, will be launched in March next year.

Published by the Malaysian Care and Concern for Humanity Organisation (Malaysia Peduli) in Bahasa Melayu and English, the book features photographs, archival materials, documents and historical records relating to the Prime Minister.

The pre-launch ceremony for the coffee table book was officiated by the Finance Minister's political secretary, Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim, here today. Also present was Malaysia Peduli chairman Noor Sham @ Ann Abu Samah.
Speaking to reporters, Muhammad Kamil said the book was important in helping younger generations understand the Prime Minister's life journey.
"I think it is very important, particularly for the younger generation, to understand the history of the Prime Minister's struggles and journey.
"These experiences have been documented in a book so that it can serve as a guide and lesson, and perhaps also as a source of reflection for society," he said.

The book traces key moments that have shaped the Prime Minister's journey, from his early years and the ideals underpinning his struggles through various challenges and changes, to his responsibilities as the country's leader and Malaysia's role on the international stage.
The publication brings together a visual record of a journey intertwined with Malaysia's social, political and historical developments.

The book was made possible through the support and cooperation of various parties, which provided guidance, access to resources, expertise and other assistance, including the National Archives of Malaysia and the Information Department of Malaysia.
bcce119a0f2366f2: NEW YORK: Fears of a potential hit to artificial-intelligence (AI) funding due to higher interest rates drove Nasdaq futures down more than 1% on Thursday, deepening a selloff in AI-related stocks.

The Nasdaq and the S&P 500 marked their biggest one-day drop since July on Wednesday, after hotter-than-expected inflation data fueled expectations of more interest rate hikes from the US Federal Reserve and sent tech stocks tumbling.

Further denting sentiment on Thursday, TSMC, the world's largest manufacturer of advanced chips, struck a cautious note for 2027 due to macroeconomic uncertainties after reporting its sixth consecutive record quarterly profit.
Reports that AI lab Anthropic reported a 45% surge in third-quarter revenue compared to the previous quarter also failed to lift investor spirits.
CoreWeave, a heavily indebted data-centre operator in the eye of the recent tech storm, fell another 6.3% in premarket trading following a 15% drop on Wednesday.
Cloud computing giant Oracle fell 2.1% after a nearly 9% drop in the previous session. The companies' bonds also came under pressure, pushing their yields to record highs.
CoreWeave and Oracle, along with other chipmakers, hyperscalers and cloud companies, looked set for a second day of sharp declines.
Nvidia fell 1.8%, while Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices dropped 3.7% and 2.3%, respectively.
"A slowdown in the AI infrastructure build-out would imply a sharp slowdown in US growth expectations," said Mohit Kumar, an economist at Jefferies.
"We expect the earnings season to justify that earnings and demand remain robust," he said, noting that Jefferies would look to take some chips off the table ahead of the midterm election.
At 5:50 am, Dow E-minis rose 165 points, or 0.32%, S&P 500 E-minis fell 21 points, or 0.27%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis lost 331.5 points, or 1.1%.
Investors will keep a close eye on producer price data at 8.30am for clues on factory inflation.
September retail sales, initial jobless claims data and several business surveys are also due to be released later in the day.
Traders are pricing in a 27% chance of a central bank rate hike later this month, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool, up from 20% a week ago.
Meanwhile, the odds of a 25-basis-point hike in December stood at 67%.

The Nasdaq has dropped more than 3% from record highs it touched last week, with concerns about higher interest rates and AI spending threatening to overshadow what is forecast to be a solid earnings season.
Analysts expect S&P 500 profits to grow 30.6% in the third quarter, according to LSEG data, with technology and energy companies doing the heavy lifting.
Shares of Rocket Lab dropped 9.7% after the space company said the inaugural launch of its new, larger Neutron rocket was delayed until next year.
fb93183fd684f409: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 15 — A female university student died after allegedly falling from a building in the hostel block of a higher education institute in Jalan Bukit Gambir, Gelugor here today.

Timur Laut district police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said the police received a phone call from the university at 8.40am informing them of the discovery of the body of a 21-year-old female student residing in the dormitory.

The student’s body was found at 7.25am by the university’s cleaning staff. She was found lying on her back on the cement floor below the dormitory block. The student, suspected of having fallen from the building, was pronounced dead at the scene.

“Investigations at the scene found no signs of criminal elements, and further examination of the victim’s body revealed several external injuries suspected to have been caused by a fall from a height,” he said in a statement today.
The victim’s body has been sent to the Penang Hospital’s Forensic Department for an autopsy, and a sudden death report (LMM) has been opened to conduct an investigation into the case. — Bernama
b6c0f2947b7eb01e: ISRAEL-GAZA BORDER, Oct 15 — Israeli opposition politician Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s main rival in upcoming elections, vowed today to defeat Hamas in Gaza if he becomes prime minister following the October 27 vote.

“Today I give a public commitment: from the moment I enter the Prime Minister’s Office, within 18 months Hamas will no longer rule the Gaza Strip,” the leader of the centre-right Yashar party said at a press conference near the war-ravaged Palestinian territory.

He said he would achieve this either by implementing US President Donald Trump’s ceasefire plan for Gaza, which provides for the gradual disarmament of Hamas and a transfer of power, or through “creative operations” by Israel’s military aimed at destroying the Palestinian movement’s military wing.
The campaign pledge is one of the strongest yet from Eisenkot, a 66-year-old former military chief.
The close-fought election will be the first since Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack on Israel, which resulted in the deaths of more than 1,200 people.

In response, Israel launched a massive offensive in Gaza that has since killed more than 74,300 people, according to the territory’s health ministry, which operates under Hamas and whose figures are generally considered reliable by the United Nations.
Eisenkot today accused Netanyahu of a “strategic failure” in Gaza, where he said “Hamas is still the sovereign... armed, arming itself, and militarily active” after three years of war.
He also reiterated a pledge to establish a state commission of inquiry to identify those responsible for any security lapses leading up to October 7, a push the government has so far resisted.
“There is a way to prevent the next disaster,” he said.

Eisenkot, like other opposition politicians, regularly accuses Netanyahu of bearing personal responsibility for the October 7 attack, notably by ignoring warnings from his security services and the United Arab Emirates, according to media reports.
Netanyahu has categorically rejected the accusations and maintains that security officials did not wake him on the morning of the attack.
Current polls show that neither Netanyahu’s bloc nor that led by Eisenkot are in a position to win the 61 seats needed to control the 120-seat parliament and form a governing coalition. — AFP
aeb9fda9b49b19aa: ISTANBUL: Istanbul was on Thursday battling to recover from flooding caused by what officials said was the heaviest rainfall in the city since records began more than 80 years ago, as the downpour continued.

The rain began lashing Turkey's largest city in earnest on Wednesday morning and intensified throughout the day, causing chaos and flash flooding, with footage showing cars being dragged away by the fast-flowing waters.
"We are talking here about the highest level of precipitation in Istanbul since records began in 1942," Istanbul governor Davut Gul said.
Two people died in the floods, one of them a 14-year-old boy who was electrocuted when he stepped into a puddle in the Balat area.
He was rushed to hospital, but medical personnel were unable to save him, officials said.
"Another three people were being treated in hospital," Gul said.

On Wednesday evening, the governor said schools would be shut across Istanbul until Monday, urging people to stay home "unless absolutely necessary" and advising those living in basement properties "to spend the night on safer, higher floors".
He advised residents to stay away from "stream beds, underpasses and other areas at risk of flooding".
Dramatic footage posted online and collated by DHA news agency showed a line of parked cars in the northern Sariyer district being pushed into the torrent of muddy water, where they were swept away.

Another showed people being hauled from the raging waters to safety through a first-floor window, while elsewhere two people with umbrellas were seen stepping into the shovel of a large mechanical digger, which took them away.

Forty-three flights bound for Istanbul Airport on the Black Sea had to be diverted, as did three flights heading for the city's Sabiha Gokcen airport on the Asian side, which also temporarily suspended take-offs due to strong winds, the transport ministry said in a statement carried by state news agency Anadolu.

Turkey's AFAD disaster agency has set up a crisis desk to manage incidents caused by the heavy rainfall, which by nightfall Wednesday had risen to 1,277 flooding incidents, 15 landslides, 47 people stranded and two roofs blown off.
The heavy rains are expected to continue over the weekend.
a1b12d6d085cc938: JAKARTA: Indonesian authorities said on Thursday they would consider offers of foreign assistance to tackle the country's biggest forest fires in over a decade after President Prabowo Subianto named a new disaster management leader.
The Southeast Asian nation is facing intense criticism as it struggles to control its most intense wildfires since 2015 after an El Niño-driven drought turned forests and land highly flammable.

The fires have been raging for months and hundreds of thousands of people have contracted respiratory illnesses in the worst-hit provinces, while the transboundary haze has also hampered air quality in neighbouring countries, forcing school closures in Malaysia and East Timor.

"The sky yesterday was very yellow ... People's activities are far reduced because of this condition. We hope there will be rain soon that will ease this problem," 46-year-old Adinata, a resident of Palangka Raya city in Central Kalimantan, told Reuters.
Dozens of residents in the city, which has been darkened by thick orange smog this week, staged a protest at the governor's office on Thursday, local news reported.
Cities in Kalimantan and Sumatra have been choked by haze due to peatland fires, which smoulder slowly beneath the surface and can re-emerge anytime, and also produce thicker smoke.

The air pollution index in the regions has far exceeded the "hazardous" level of 300 with the Katingan district of Central Kalimantan registering a reading of nearly 1,600 earlier on Thursday, while the provincial capital Palangka Raya recorded nearly 1,300.
Prabowo named army general Kristomei Sianturi as the new head of disaster mitigation agency BNPB, the main body in charge of the firefighting efforts.
"I will assess our assets and see what kind of foreign aid we can accelerate," Sianturi said after his inauguration, adding he has been tasked to contain the wildfires "as soon as possible."
Malaysia last month had offered three helicopters and an aircraft to help put out the wildfires, but an official earlier this week said Indonesia is "still able to handle" the issue.

The president also named forestry ministry official Satyawan Pudyatmoko as chief of a newly formed peatland and mangrove body on Thursday, tasking him with restoring the country's peatland ecosystem and preventing repeated wildfires.
"We will restore peatland ecosystems to their former condition," he told reporters. "There are a number of peatland areas that are being prioritised and the president doesn't want any more fires."

Peatland protection group Pantau Gambut estimated that out of 24 million hectares of Indonesian peatland, 16 million hectares have been made more fire-prone as a result of ecosystem damage, including extensive deforestation and the depletion of water tables.

A 2024 study conducted by Pantau Gambut showed that only 3% of the peatland damaged by fires over the 2015 to 2019 period has been restored into forest, while 54% was converted into monoculture plantations, mainly oil palm.

A food estate project in the 1990s was among the causes of peatland degradation, deputy food minister Hanif Faisol Nurofiq said, and the government is aiming to drill wells to rewet peatlands and improve water canal management.
Thesa, a 19-year-old university student in Palangka Raya who has been experiencing dizziness due to haze, sought help at a volunteer organization providing oxygen for people exposed to toxic air.
"We are being exposed to the smoke everyday... and there is only a fan at my boarding room (to alleviate the smoke)."
5271c79ceb4f6986: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 15 — The chairman of a statutory body in Penang pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to 15 charges of accepting bribes totalling more than RM800,000 between June 2025 and July this year.

Datuk Dr Shaik Hussein Mydin, 53, is accused of corruptly receiving RM847,107.61 through Aliran Ilham Sdn Bhd (AISB) in multiple transactions from ATSH Management Sdn Bhd (ATSH) director Datuk R. Albert Suresh. The alleged bribes ranged from RM45.51 to RM244,620.

The payments were allegedly received as an inducement for appointing ATSH as a subcontractor to AISB for a RM23.27 million project to construct a 10-storey hostel block and facilities using the Industrialised Building System at Institut Kemahiran Tinggi PERDA in Bukit Panchor, Seberang Perai Selatan.
The alleged offences took place at a bank in Jalan Perda Selatan, Bandar Perda, in Seberang Perai Tengah, between June 26, 2025, and July 9, 2026.

The charges were brought under Section 16(a)(A) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009 (Act 694), which provides for a maximum prison term of 20 years and a fine of at least five times the value of the gratification involved, or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.

Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) deputy public prosecutors Lim Jin Hong and Nurnajihatul Idayu Mohd Azuyar proposed bail of RM1 million, with additional conditions requiring the accused to surrender his passport, report to the MACC office monthly and refrain from interfering with prosecution witnesses.

Shaik Hussein was represented by a seven-member legal team led by Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, comprising Datuk Hasnal Rezua Merican, Mohd Shahrullah Khan, Simon Tan, Dr Shamsher Singh Thind, Muzzammil Merican and Intan Nur Alia Nodzri.

Amer Hamzah objected to the proposed bail amount, describing it as excessive and arguing that the prosecution had not provided sufficient factual grounds to justify the sum as necessary to ensure his client’s attendance in court.

Judge Irwan Suainbon granted the accused bail of RM300,000, subject to reporting to the MACC office once every two months and the other conditions proposed by the prosecution, and fixed Jan 8, 2027, for the submission of documents.
The court also allowed the accused to apply for the temporary release of his passport for specific periods and purposes, should the need arise. — Bernama
66cd3ee9750f0b84: Hackers who broke into the UK's Legal Aid Agency last year stole records dating back nearly five decades, the government has admitted, revealing the breach was far more extensive than previously thought. The Legal Aid Agency said on Wednesday that around 250,000 records stolen in the April 2025 attack date from before 2007, including one going back to 1978. That's much further back than the agency previously estimated ­­– it initially said the stolen data covered legal aid applications, claims, and payments from 2007. Most of the newly identified records date from the 1990s and 2000s, with only a “fractionally small number” originating before 1990. Still, the discovery raises an awkward question about just how much historical personal information was sitting in government systems when the attackers came knocking. That wasn't the only surprise in the stolen data, as the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) has also discovered that hackers accessed information from HM Prison and Probation Service (HMPPS), including names, dates of birth, nationalities, and case reference numbers for offenders supervised by probation services between 2010 and 2017. The government says the probation records concern a relatively small number of offenders, with more than 99 percent of the affected data relating to people under supervision in 2016 and 2017. It stressed that none of the stolen probation information relates to victims of crime. The latest revelations come almost 18 months after the Legal Aid Agency disclosed that criminals had accessed and downloaded a significant amount of sensitive personal information. The agency first detected the intrusion on April 23, 2025, but officials didn't establish the scale of the compromise until May 16. The government subsequently took the LAA's online services offline, leaving lawyers struggling to access the systems they needed to submit claims and manage cases. The disruption dragged on for months, with the agency's troubled return to service in December leaving legal aid providers battling delays and ongoing technical problems. Further forensic work has now revealed that the data theft goes back much further than officials originally believed. The compromised information varies by individual but could include names, addresses, dates of birth, National Insurance numbers, financial details, and information about legal proceedings. Some records also contain details of criminal charges, pleas, convictions, and sentences. Among the older material are records relating to legal aid benefit assessments dating from 1978 to 2012, and payments made under the Very High Cost Cases scheme between 1981 and 2004. The government cautioned that the presence of historical records doesn’t mean that everyone who applied for legal aid before 2007 had their information stolen, nor does the 250,000 figure represent a confirmed number of affected individuals. Explaining why it has taken so long to pin down the extent of the theft, the MoJ said the attackers stole information spread across several complex systems, much of it unstructured, fragmented, or incomplete. "Because of our increased capability to identify data, we have developed a more complete understanding of the information compromised," the agency said. The government says it has no indication that the stolen information has been published or shared, although that offers little certainty to anyone whose personal details may now be in criminal hands. Since the attack, the MoJ says it has tightened authentication and access controls, improved security monitoring, addressed vulnerabilities and begun retiring or isolating higher-risk technology. Work to modernize its legacy systems is also underway. The question of why records stretching back to the 1970s remained accessible in the first place is one the latest update does not answer. ®
1aa0f61369207759: PETALING JAYA: A 19-year-old woman has been sentenced to a month in jail and fined RM5,000 by the Kota Kinabalu magistrates' court for inducing her own miscarriage.
Magistrate Marilyn Kelvin convicted the woman after she pleaded guilty to a charge under Section 312 of the Penal Code, The Borneo Post reported.
She was also ordered to serve eight months in jail if she failed to pay the fine.
The offence took place at a rented house in Kota Kinabalu on May 15.
According to the facts of the case, the student, who was 15 weeks' pregnant, had sought treatment at a hospital's emergency unit after experiencing bleeding.
She had taken 11 tablets of 200mcg Misoprostol (Cytotec) orally and inserted three more tablets into her vagina.
Investigations found that she had taken the medication to terminate the pregnancy because she was not ready to become a mother. She and her boyfriend had agreed to the abortion.
Jagnesh Jaya represented the woman, while deputy public prosecutor Ronnie Anthony prosecuted.
61b24edd6221e9bb: PETALING JAYA: An opposition politician from Mindanao allegedly funded the chartering of a private jet used to transport 521kg of methamphetamine seized in Laos, according to the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA).
PDEA spokesman Joseph Frederick Calulut said the agency had identified the alleged financier but was withholding the person's identity as investigations were ongoing.

“We have identified the financier behind this drug operation. This politician is based in the south, in Mindanao,” Calulut told reporters on Thursday, according to Makati City-based news outlet Inquirer.Net.
Calulut cited operational security and protocols that prohibited naming suspects before formal charges are filed with the department of justice.
The drugs were allegedly intended for transport aboard a private jet chartered for US$49,500.

Last week, Bukit Aman narcotics crime investigation department director Hussein Omar Khan said a Filipino national, believed to be the mastermind of a drug smuggling syndicate, had booked the private jet about a week before the seizure on Sept 23.
Hussein said the individual had engaged a private aviation company, owned by two Malaysian pilots and two Singaporeans, for a flight from Laos to Manila, with the cargo declared as vape products.
He said information about the declared cargo was obtained from the flight manifest secured in Subang and from Laotian authorities.

The jet had departed Subang for Luang Prabang International Airport in Laos without any drugs on board. The 521kg of crystal methamphetamine, packed in 500 packages and believed to be destined for Manila, was allegedly loaded onto the aircraft after it arrived in Laos.
Thirteen people, including the pilot, co-pilot, Filipino passengers and airport and ground service personnel, were detained by Laotian authorities to assist in the investigation.
Meanwhile, Calulut said the PDEA investigation had expanded beyond two Filipino suspects previously identified by their aliases, Fahad and Boyet.
“We have also identified their associates,” he said, without specifying how many people were involved.
Fahad has been arrested by Laotian authorities and is expected to face charges, while Boyet was last reported to be in Hong Kong.
be75dc4992b43cee: RIYADH, Oct 15 — The Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis today said it had intercepted a cruise missile in the Medina region — home to one of Islam’s holiest cities, but the Houthis denied carrying out any such attack.
“Interception and destruction of a cruise missile in the Medina region,” coalition spokesman Turki Al-Malki wrote on X, with the statement also published by state media.
The Houthis quickly responded by saying they did not target the region today, and had previously vowed to spare the holy cities of Medina and Mecca.

Saudi Arabia has in recent days come under sustained attack from the Houthis, including a strike on Riyadh’s international airport that was the kingdom’s deadliest in years, as the war with the group escalates.
Riyadh has hit back with strikes against the Iran-backed group’s stronghold in the Yemeni capital Sanaa.
Medina, the burial place of the Prophet Mohammed and home to the Prophet’s Mosque, is one of Islam’s holiest cities alongside Mecca.
The Houthis have vowed to continue targeting airports and other sites across Saudi Arabia but on Sunday said Mecca and Medina would be spared.

“The Yemeni armed forces confirm that they have not carried out any operation today targeting Saudi territory, and that the Saudi enemy’s claims of an attack on Medina are a shameless and brazen lie,” Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree wrote on X today.

Yesterday the Houthis said they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco, with Saudi officials reporting a strike on a building in an area housing the energy giant’s operations centre.
The Saudi-led coalition has supported Yemen’s government militarily against the Houthis since 2015 in a long-running civil war that has created a humanitarian crisis. — AFP
04849d4d7df6c2b3: PETALING JAYA: Amanah is confident of defending the Bukit Katil seat in next month’s Melaka state election, despite political analyst Ong Kian Ming’s prediction that Barisan Nasional (BN) could take the seat.
Melaka Amanah chief Ashraf Mukhlis Minghat said the confidence was based on incumbent Adly Zahari's service record, citing more than 280 initiatives over the last term.

“We have done our best in serving the people. It is now up to the voters to assess our performance and decide. Amanah's election machinery in Bukit Katil is in optimal condition, and efforts to engage voters are already under way,” he told FMT.

Ong had previously predicted that BN could retain the 21 seats it won in the 2021 state election and potentially pick up three to four more. The predictions included BN wresting Bukit Katil from Adly as well as winning the DAP stronghold of Ayer Keroh.

Adly, a former Melaka chief minister, first won Bukit Katil in the 2018 general election with a 3,159-vote majority in a three-cornered contest. He retained the seat in the 2021 Melaka state election, but his majority shrank to 1,057 votes in a four-cornered fight.
Ashraf dismissed the former DAP leader’s forecast as a personal opinion.
"Everyone is entitled to their own perspectives, but Amanah has never taken any of these predictions lightly and always strives to step up the groundwork to reach more voters," said Ashraf.
Ashraf also said Pakatan Harapan (PH) had a chance of returning to run Melaka even if it faced both BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN), claiming the split between PAS and Bersatu had weakened PN.
“PH still has an opportunity to return to government in Melaka, despite facing BN and PN. The voters are smart and will not easily be swayed by the 'blue wave'.
“After what happened in Negeri Sembilan, it is clear that the blue wave itself cannot solve the problems it created.”
He hoped PH’s record of running Melaka from 2018 to 2020 would be considered by the 700,000 voters.
3840b71408c1bdaf: KUALA LUMPUR: An MP has asked how the government intends to prevent victims of drink-driving accidents from receiving double compensation if they are paid under the proposed amendments to the Road Transport Act 1987 and later win damages in a civil suit.

“How will the government ensure victims do not receive double compensation without affecting their rights to claim fair damages?” asked Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor) while debating the 2027 budget in the Dewan Rakyat.

While he welcomed plans to amend the law to make drivers convicted of serious offences compensate accident victims or their families, Ramkarpal asked how compensation amounts would be determined and whether medical bills, lost income, permanent injuries and long-term care needs would be considered.
He also wanted to know whether a standard formula would be used or if each case would be assessed separately.
Speaking to FMT later, Ramkarpal clarified that he was seeking clarification on how the proposed system would work, rather than expressing an opinion on it.
At present, victims of accidents caused by drivers under the influence of drugs or alcohol can seek compensation through insurance claims or by suing those responsible.
Through a civil suit, victims can claim compensation for medical bills, lost income, long-term care and other losses. If both sides cannot agree on an amount, the court decides on the sum payable.

Existing law also allows courts to order convicted offenders to compensate victims if prosecutors request it. Victims can still sue for damages, but any compensation already paid under the criminal case is taken into account to prevent double payment.
The proposed changes to the Road Transport Act aim to make compensation part of the criminal case against the driver, allowing victims to seek payment without filing a separate civil suit.

In July, transport minister Loke Siew Fook said the proposed scheme would not affect victims' rights to make insurance claims or sue for damages. He said judges would determine compensation based on victims' injuries and losses, as well as the offender’s ability to pay.

Earlier today, Loke also told the Dewan Rakyat that the government was studying whether it could seize the assets of motorists convicted of serious traffic offences who failed to compensate road accident victims and their families.
He said the government was also considering whether offenders who failed to pay could face heavier fines or jail terms under other laws.
6459c28ff601cff6: KUALA LUMPUR: Seorang saksi pihak pendakwaan, yang membuat laporan polis terhadap filem kontroversi 'Mentega Terbang' pada 2023, memberi keterangan di mahkamah majistret bahawa filem itu tidak menyebabkan beliau mempertikaikan akidahnya sebagai seorang Islam.
Yamna Ismail berkata beliau sudah pun mempelajari tentang penjelmaan semula (reinkarnasi) daripada sumber lain, termasuk bahan bacaan, filem dan anime, sebelum menonton 'Mentega Terbang'.
Beliau berkata demikian semasa pemeriksaan silang oleh peguam bela, Zaid Malek.
Zaid: Walaupun filem ini menyebut tentang penjelmaan semula, anda tetap seorang Muslim?
Yamna: Betul.
Zaid: Jadi, filem ini tidak menyebabkan anda terpesong (akidah)?
Yamna: Tidak.
Suri rumah berusia 39 tahun itu memberi keterangan pada hari keempat perbicaraan membabitkan pengarah filem berkenaan, Khairi Anwar Jailani, dan penerbit iaitu Tan Meng Kheng.

Apabila ditanya sama ada orang lain dalam masyarakat majmuk di negara ini juga boleh mempelajari tentang penjelmaan semula daripada sumber lain seperti beliau, Yamna berkata: "Saya hanya boleh bercakap bagi pihak saya sendiri. Saya tidak pasti tentang orang lain."
Beliau juga tidak bersetuju dengan cadangan Zaid bahawa filem itu tidak boleh menyesatkan umat Islam semata-mata kerana ia membincangkan tentang penjelmaan semula.

Yamna sebelum ini memberi keterangan bahawa filem itu menyinggung perasaan beliau sebagai seorang Islam, dengan memetik beberapa adegan yang menyentuh soal akidah, penjelmaan semula, prasangka, dwistandard terhadap Islam dan perbandingan agama.
Semasa prosiding hari ini, beliau tidak bersetuju dengan cadangan Zaid bahawa beliau membuat laporan polis untuk mempertahankan Islam dan bukan kerana tersinggung dengan filem tersebut.
Bagaimanapun, apabila Zaid merujuk kepada laporan polisnya, beliau mengubah jawapannya dan bersetuju dengan cadangan Zaid sebelum itu.
Beliau juga mengaku tidak menggunakan perkataan 'tersinggung' di dalam laporan itu.
Zaid turut mempersoalkan dakwaannya dalam pernyataan saksi bahawa beliau telah menonton keseluruhan filem itu pada 26 Februari 2023.
Apabila ditanya platform yang digunakan untuk menontonnya, Yamna berkata beliau menontonnya di YouTube menggunakan telefon bimbit.
Zaid: Saya mencadangkan kepada anda bahawa filem itu tidak tersedia di YouTube pada tarikh tersebut.
Yamna: Saya setuju.
Beliau tidak menjawab apabila ditanya sama ada beliau telah memberikan keterangan palsu dalam pernyataan saksi.
Khairi, 34, yang juga penulis skrip, dan Tan, 39, dituduh pada 17 Jan 2024 mengikut Seksyen 298 Kanun Keseksaan atas pertuduhan sengaja melukakan perasaan agama orang lain.
Filem tersebut ditayangkan pada 28 Nov 2021 sebelum Kementerian Dalam Negeri mengharamkannya pada 1 Sept 2023.
Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Nor Azizah Aling and Nadia Izhar hadir bagi pihak pendakwaan.
Perbicaraan di hadapan Majistret Heng Yi Min bersambung pada 25 Januari tahun depan.
2df0f2eea7b00435: KUALA LUMPUR: Cadangan pindaan Perlembagaan berkaitan pengehadan tempoh jawatan perdana menteri serta pengasingan peranan peguam negara dan pendakwa raya menjadi antara perkara utama yang dirunding dan dibincangkan dalam Mesyuarat Majlis Raja-Raja Ke-273.

Mesyuarat dua hari yang bermula semalam di Istana Negara dipengerusikan oleh Sultan Perak Sultan Nazrin Shah manakala Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim berangkat hadir pada hari kedua dengan diiringi Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim.

Menurut kenyataan yang dikeluarkan oleh Pejabat Penyimpan Mohor Besar Raja-Raja hari ini, majlis memperhalusi Kertas Untuk Merundingi Majlis Raja-Raja Berkenaan Rang Undang-Undang (RUU) Perlembagaan (Pindaan) 2026 Mengenai Pengehadan Tempoh Jawatan Perdana Menteri.

Selain itu, Majlis Raja-Raja turut disembah maklum mengenai Kertas Untuk Memaklumkan Majlis Raja-Raja Berkenaan RUU Perlembagaan (Pindaan) (No 2) 2026 Berkaitan Pengasingan Peranan Peguam Negara Dan Pendakwa Raya serta cadangan pindaan Seksyen 97 Akta Kanak-Kanak 2001.

b602fe5eed1badec: PETALING JAYA: CTOS Digital Bhd hit a new all-time low today after major research houses downgraded the credit reporting agency following a major cybersecurity incident.
Its shares tumbled as much as 17% or 8.5 sen to 41.5 sen before closing half a sen higher at 42 sen, valuing the group at RM929 million. A total of 21.4 million shares were traded.
This broke its previous record low of 47.5 sen set earlier this week. The stock has lost about 40% of its value year to date and is trading 62% below its July 2021 IPO price of RM1.10.
CTOS first disclosed the cybersecurity incident on Sept 23, saying unauthorised access had occurred in an environment supporting its consumer business.

Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) subsequently suspended its Central Credit Reference Information System (CCRIS) which collects credit and loan data, disrupting some of its credit reporting services, including CTOS Score and related products.

CTOS said on Tuesday that the cybersecurity breach is expected to reduce FY2026’s net profit by RM12 million and revenue by RM16 million. The estimates assume some services remain unavailable until the third week of October.

Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB), Kenanga Investment Bank and CIMB Securities have downgraded their recommendations in recent days and slashed their target prices. They also warned of material impact to CTOS' earnings from the suspension of services.
In a note today, HLIB said the cybersecurity incident is set to “inflict a meaningful earnings drag” on CTOS.
It downgraded its call on the stock from “buy” to “hold”, with a lower target price (TP) of 50 sen. It also cut its FY2026-2028 earnings forecasts by 18%, 15%, and 14% respectively.
The bank said restoration of its services “doesn’t mean immediate normalisation”, warning CTOS faces an even longer road ahead to rebuild client confidence.
“In our view, restoring the system may be quicker than restoring customer confidence,” it stressed.
Kenanga has downgraded its call on CTOS to “market perform” from “outperform”, and lowered its TP to 48 sen from 83 sen.
It cited heightened operational, regulatory and reputational risks, weaker earnings visibility, and the possibility of customers switching to rival credit bureaus.
It also said the cybersecurity incident could cut CTOS' FY2026 core net profit by RM22 million if its Score and CCRIS-related services remain unavailable until end-December.
CIMB Securities said the prolonged service disruption has potential longer-term implications for customer retention and cybersecurity costs on top of weaker earnings visibility.
It added slower transaction volume recovery, potential customer migration to alternative providers and higher cybersecurity spending could weigh on company earnings next year.

CTOS' largest shareholder with a 20.87% stake is private equity firm Creador, through Jade Vine Sdn Bhd, followed by the Employees Provident Fund (20.68%), Aberdeen Group plc (14.89%) and Retirement Fund (Incorporated) (KWAP) (9.04%).

45f36e5f71bf19fa: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 15 — The Court of Appeal today upheld a 30-year jail sentence and 12 strokes of the cane imposed on a former trader for murdering his step-brother and concealing the body in a cement-filled drum.

A three-judge panel comprising Justices Datuk Noorin Badaruddin, Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar unanimously dismissed Mohamad Zamhuri Azami’s appeal against his conviction and sentence.
The panel also dismissed the prosecution’s appeal to impose the death penalty on the 31-year-old accused.
Delivering the court’s unanimous decision, Justice Noorin said the sentence imposed by the High Court was appropriate and did not warrant appellate intervention.
“We also find no sufficient grounds to replace the sentence with the death penalty or a 40-year prison term, as requested by the prosecution,” she said.

Justice Noorin said the possibility of an argument or altercation between the appellant and the deceased did not, in itself, establish that the fatal act was justified under the defence of private defence.

She also said the prosecution had successfully established the necessary intention through the evidence presented, leaving no grounds to substitute the conviction with one under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
On May 13 last year, the Alor Setar High Court found Mohamad Zamhuri guilty of murdering Mohd Hasnul Nizar Khairul Anuar, 34, and sentenced him to 30 years in prison and 12 strokes of the cane.
The offence was committed at their home in Kampung Padang Hassan, Bukit Pinang, Alor Setar, Kedah, at 7.15pm on March 6, 2020.

According to the facts of the case, the appellant led police to the location where the victim’s body was concealed in a blue plastic drum filled with cement outside the house. Police also seized a meat-cleaving knife.

During today’s proceedings, defence counsel Ai Cha Ran argued that his client had not intended to kill his step-brother, claiming that the deceased had attacked him during an altercation and that he had acted in self-defence.
He further submitted that the evidence supported only a charge of culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code.

However, Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Aqilah Syaza Ariffin argued that the pathologist’s testimony showed that the victim’s injuries, particularly a long and deep incised wound to the neck, were inconsistent with the defence’s account of a fight or struggle. — Bernama

949564570609f673: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The ringgit closed higher against the weakening greenback today as investors assessed market conditions ahead of the release of Malaysia’s advance gross domestic product (GDP) estimates for the third quarter of 2026 (3Q 2026) tomorrow.

He said in the fixed-income market, the 10-year US Treasury yield fell by 10 basis points to 5.09 per cent, reflecting increased demand for safe-haven assets following the sell-off in technology stocks, particularly artificial intelligence (AI)-related companies.

“Meanwhile, cautious remarks from Federal Reserve officials have tempered expectations of an imminent interest rate hike despite the elevated inflation reading, contributing to the US dollar’s weakness,” said Mohd Afzanizam.
At the close, the ringgit traded lower against a basket of major currencies.

It eased against the Japanese yen to 2.5869/5892 from 2.5751/5781 at yesterday’s close, decreased against the euro to 4.5761/5801 from 4.5673/5723 and inched up against the British pound to 5.4101/4147 from 5.4132/4192.

4f3f7837dc03a488: Welcome, once again, to PWNED, the weekly column where we gawk at organizations that have made serious security mistakes. Normally, we’re talking about businesses or maybe the odd school that messes up, but today we’re writing about a serious IT screwup in the world’s most powerful military. Have a story about someone leaving a gaping hole in their network? Share it with us at pwned@sitpub.com. Anonymity is available upon request. Today’s tale comes from Justin Henkel, the CISO of IT monitoring and service company SolarWinds. Henkel previously worked in IT security for the Air Force and one day in the early 2000s saw a practice that just wouldn’t fly today. Before USB drives became popular, burning CDs with mission data was the modus operandi, and those discs were put in both unclassified and classified systems. “They would write a CD, and then they would take that CD and then put it in a classified system and do the remainder of the mission planning,” Henkel told us. “Then they would take that disc and then put it in the airplane.” Inside the airplane, the data on the CD would help the pilot navigate and contain information about threats they might encounter. Later, when thumb drives became a thing, pilots used them instead of discs. “They didn't really think about the overall impact of classified versus unclassified systems,” Henkel said of the pilots. “Using the same device for both, they didn’t understand that you could read and write onto a USB drive with malware. [They were] not really understanding the overall threat picture.” According to Henkel, Air Force personnel would buy their flash drives from local vendors rather than sourcing them from official military contractors. If they were in Afghanistan, those drives could literally come from a store in Kabul. And it wasn’t exactly the equivalent of Best Buy. “It was more difficult to bring a US-based computer into the nation than it was just to buy local,” he said. “So they were just going out into the local market in Kabul or whatever city that they were out [in]. And I used to do this: go out, make relationships with the local vendors. ‘Hey I need 100 USB sticks.’” Unfortunately, enemies of the US noticed and soon started selling infected USB drives to local vendors in the Middle East. Henkel knew that using a sneakernet with classified systems was a recipe for disaster. It’s just that no one would listen to him. “It was just a shock,” he told us. “I was a young 22-year-old guy, very junior in the overall rank system, trying to tell colonels and majors that what they’re doing is a violation.” In 2008, the US Department of Defense was infected by malware after somebody attached an infected USB flash drive to a laptop with access to US Central Command. The worm, dubbed Agent.BTZ, could collect information from infected computers and communicate with remote servers. A 2016 report from the FBI and DHS attributed the malware to one or more Russian groups. It took the Pentagon 14 months to scrub it from its systems. It took this attack for the Pentagon to wise up in 2008 and ban the use of USB drives, instead forcing data transfers to go through more secure systems. Eventually, in 2010, the drives were allowed again under certain circumstances. ®

292481240ddbf402: A Japanese consortium wants to ease the datacenter space crunch by putting servers afloat – but keeping them moored safely alongside port quays. The group comprises shipping and logistics corporation NYK Line, engineering biz NTT Facilities, renewable energy developer Eurus Energy, and MUFG Bank. The quartet has also considered facilities farther out at sea, where they could draw on renewable energy sources such as offshore wind. Others are exploring wave power, including Oregon-based Panthalassa. However, the fab four acknowledge that offshore deployments still face practical hurdles, including maintenance access, high-capacity telecoms links, and independent power supplies. Keeping the floating facilities alongside a quay would let them use existing port infrastructure and nearby generation while the group works toward deployments well beyond the coast. Like others eyeing the waterfront, the consortium reckons bobbing bit barns could help meet growing compute demand without competing for scarce development land, though they would still need somewhere to plug in. We asked the consortium what capacity it expects the facilities to have, and when it anticipates these might be operational, but hadn't received a response at time of publication. NYK Line will oversee development, NTT Facilities will assess the designs, construction, and operation. Eurus Energy will explore renewable power supply, and MUFG Bank will consider financing related ventures. The consortium previously signed a memorandum of understanding with the city of Yokohama for a renewable-powered demonstration at the port. Testing began in March this year. The four may find they face competition in the floating compute farm stakes. Samsung Heavy Industries plans to dip a toe in, saying it expects to have its first facility operational by the second calendar quarter of 2028. ®
70c732a9a0197878: In this age of rising electricity demand, people are trying to squeeze every last bit of power out of every power plant possible.

Over the past few weeks, there’s been big news about nuclear power plants trying to do just that. Constellation, the largest nuclear operator in the US, announced plans to add nearly a gigawatt of new capacity across 11 existing nuclear reactors at six plants. And on October 5, the Department of Energy awarded a $4.2 billion loan to Vistra for previously announced upgrades at three plants.
Pushing existing reactors to produce more could help provide more clean power for data centers, quickly. But just how much additional power can we count on?

Upgrading equipment at existing nuclear power plants can allow them to reach a higher capacity; the process is called a power uprate. Operators have been doing this since the 1970s in the US, but it’s been less common in recent years as demand for electricity plateaued and cheap natural gas put financial pressure on nuclear power plants. Some plants closed, and putting in more money to produce more electricity didn’t make much sense at others. Between 2001 and 2010, the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission approved over 80 uprates. Between 2011 and 2020, the number was 33.

But with the rise of AI and the related boom in electricity demand, there’s been a shift. We’re seeing shuttered plants like Palisades and Three Mile Island race to reopen. And existing plants are looking to uprate again.

Some uprates are minor, involving changes to instrument setpoints or calculations at the plant. But more major overhauls, which can boost reactor power by as much as 20%, require replacing plant equipment.

Generally, uprates involve using fuel that’s more highly enriched, or a higher volume of fresh fuel, in the nuclear reactor. That helps produce more steam, which is used to turn a turbine and generate electricity. To handle that additional energy, the main turbines and equipment such as pumps, motors, generators, and transformers are upgraded.

The most recent major uprate approved in the US was for three reactors at the Browns Ferry nuclear power plant in Alabama. A $475 million project saw that plant expand its power capacity by 14% between 2018 and 2019.

Things could pick up soon, though. Constellation announced plans this week to spend more than $4.3 billion on uprates to 11 reactors. The additional electricity will be enough to power roughly 700,000 US homes.

Behind it all? Big Tech money. Google agreed to buy electricity from these plants, and the 20-year agreement was a major factor in making the uprates happen. As Joe Dominguez, Constellation’s CEO, told the New York Times: “These are capital intensive, labor intensive projects that require a different price point than the market trades at, frankly.”

Also in the last few weeks, the US Department of Energy shared that it will commit over $4 billion to help finance upgrades and modernization for Vistra nuclear power plants across Pennsylvania and Ohio. Those projects will add 433 megawatts of power capacity, and Meta has already signed on to buy electricity from the plants in a long-term deal.

A note about cost: On a per-kilowatt basis, that Constellation project is less expensive than building a new reactor, but it’s still more expensive than building a new utility-scale solar farm with energy storage or a combined-cycle natural-gas plant.

Even at this high cost, uprates are in high demand. Today, the US nuclear fleet has roughly 98 gigawatts of total power capacity. Depending on who you ask, there’s somewhere between three and eight additional gigawatts on the table from uprates. A pretty significant chunk of the potential uprates in the US are already accounted for—the NRC already expects applications to add 2.4 gigawatts of power to reactors through 2032.

It’s crucial to put these plans (and the total potential for uprates in the US) in perspective, though. PJM, the grid operator that covers much of the East Coast, expects about 30 gigawatts of additional peak demand because of AI by 2030. All the possible nationwide nuclear uprates would cover just a fraction of that.

Making the most of existing nuclear reactors is a relatively easy win at a time when we need all the zero-emissions power we can get. But there’s still a lot of demand, and if we want more nuclear power to meet it, eventually that will require actually building new reactors.
This article is from The Spark, MIT Technology Review’s weekly climate newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Wednesday, sign up here.
1ef7873a373f9426: LONDON, Oct 15 — Barbie has honoured Celine Dion by creating a new signature doll in her image, PA Media/dpa reported.
